---
title: "Examples"
---

The package ships three example models from CmdStanR, with their data: `logistic`, a logistic regression, and `schools` and `schools_ncp`, the eight schools hierarchical model in its centered and non-centered forms. The data are CmdStanR's own published example data, and the eight schools values are Rubin's (1981) estimates, the same as in [schools.csv](https://github.com/phpstats/datasets#schools). The repository's `examples/` directory has the small programs used in these docs.

## Bundled models

`cmdstanr_example()` compiles an example, fits it with its bundled data, and returns the fit. The first argument names the example, and the second the method: `sample` (the default), `optimize`, `laplace`, `variational`, `pathfinder`, or `diagnose`. Other arguments are passed to the method. The executable is built in the directory set by the `cmdstanphp_example_dir` option, or in `cmdstanphp-examples` under the system temporary directory. `print_example_program()` prints the Stan program.

```php
use function CmdStan\cmdstanr_example;
use function CmdStan\print_example_program;

print_example_program('schools_ncp');

$fit = cmdstanr_example(
    'schools_ncp',
    seed: 123,
    show_messages: false,
);
$rows = $fit->summary(
    ['mu', 'tau'],
    measures: ['mean', 'sd', 'rhat', 'ess_bulk'],
);
echo "variable   mean    sd   rhat  ess_bulk\n";
foreach ($rows as $r) {
    printf(
        "%-8s %6.2f %5.2f %6.3f %9.0f\n",
        $r['variable'],
        $r['mean'],
        $r['sd'],
        $r['rhat'],
        $r['ess_bulk'],
    );
}

$warnings = $fit->diagnosticWarnings();
echo $warnings ? implode("\n", $warnings) : 'No warnings';
echo "\n";
```

```stan
data {
  int<lower=1> J;
  vector<lower=0>[J] sigma;
  vector[J] y;
}
parameters {
  real mu;
  real<lower=0> tau;
  vector[J] theta_raw;
}
transformed parameters {
  vector[J] theta = mu + tau * theta_raw;
}
model {
  target += normal_lpdf(tau | 0, 10);
  target += normal_lpdf(mu | 0, 10);
  target += normal_lpdf(theta_raw | 0, 1);
  target += normal_lpdf(y | theta, sigma);
}
```

```text
variable   mean    sd   rhat  ess_bulk
mu         6.61  4.26  1.001      3502
tau        4.71  3.65  1.000      1749
No warnings
```

The centered form, `schools`, samples the same posterior with `theta` as a parameter. With the same seed it produces divergent transitions in every chain:

```php
$fit = cmdstanr_example(
    'schools',
    seed: 123,
    show_messages: false,
);
echo implode("\n", $fit->diagnosticWarnings()), "\n";
```

```text
Chain 1: 73 divergent transitions.
Chain 2: 74 divergent transitions.
Chain 2: E-BFMI below 0.3.
Chain 3: 25 divergent transitions.
Chain 4: 8 divergent transitions.
```

The [MCMC guide](mcmc.qmd#check-convergence) explains these warnings. Outputs are from CmdStan 2.40.0 on macOS (arm64). Other CmdStan versions and platforms can give different draws for the same seed.

## Programs in the repository

The `examples/` directory of the [repository](https://github.com/phpstats/CmdStanPHP/tree/main/examples) holds:

- `bernoulli.stan` and `bernoulli.php`, the model from [Getting started](getting-started.qmd) and a script that samples it with CmdStan's own published example data, `examples/bernoulli/bernoulli.data.json`. Run `php examples/bernoulli.php` from a clone of the repository after `composer install`.
- `generated.stan`, the Bernoulli model with a posterior prediction, used in [Generated quantities](generated-quantities.qmd).
- `normal.stan`, a one-parameter normal model, used in [Log density and model methods](log-density.qmd).
